scope: read the 2697 gamestate constructor to learn what our own server must emit

verified_facts.preconditions: the function returns early unless BOTH CODOL_NetworkSessionReady(remoteAddress) and CODOL_ClientStatsUpload(clientNum) are non-NULL, which is why the bridge needs --fake-stats before a real client ever gets a gamestate
verified_facts.shape: it builds a msg_t from byte msgBuffer[MAX_MSGLEN], writes the gamestate service opcode and payload, then hands it to the netchan transmit path
verified_facts.guards: it also calls PHandler_Event(PLUGINS_ONPLAYERGOTAUTHINFO), checks ban state, and handles unsent fragments before writing
verified_facts.CODOL_branch: the CODOL_SERVER branch records previous state/gamestateSent/messageNum/reliableSent before building, and sets gamestateMessageNum from the outgoing sequence

why_this_matters_for_our_server: a gamestate is not a single fixed blob: it carries the map/config strings and player state, and its size depends on the map and settings
the client will only consume it after the session/stats preconditions are satisfied on the server side, so our own server must answer stats before sending gamestate
because the 1649370 client treats in-band headers as plaintext, our outbound packets can start as plaintext seq(4)+body and be validated by observing whether the client's messageAck advances
plan: capture the first in-band datagram the 2697 dedrun sends to a real 1649370 client (length + first bytes) with forward --dump-in, to size the gamestate we must imitate
emit a minimal plaintext packet of that length with an svc opcode guess, and watch the client's messageAck for a reaction
if the client ignores it, mirror the 2697 outbound cipher instead of plaintext
not_yet_done: no outbound gamestate has been emitted by our server yet
the svc opcode for gamestate in this build has not been confirmed from a live capture
